title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only classify entire documents and cannot localize which tokens are anomalous. The authors introduce token-level text anomaly detection and propose TokenCore, a memory-bank framework that embeds tokens with BERT (max-pooling subwords to words), stores normal token embeddings, and scores anomalies by nearest-neighbor distance, with mean aggregation for document-level scores. On three new token-annotated benchmarks (SMS spam, restaurant reviews, grammar errors), TokenCore achieves the best average AUROC among 7 methods at both token and document levels.

requirements.stmt: Use pre-trained BERT-base-uncased as the embedding backbone for all methods.
requirements.quote: All the methods operate on BERT-base-uncased embeddings with max pooling aggregation.

requirements.stmt: Aggregate subword embeddings to word-level token embeddings via element-wise max pooling, not first-subword or average pooling.
requirements.quote: we propose using max pooling to aggregate subword embeddings

requirements.stmt: Construct a memory bank M containing word-level embeddings of all tokens from normal training samples.
requirements.quote: we extract word-level embeddings from all normal samples in the training set and store them in a memory bank

requirements.stmt: Score each test token by the distance to its nearest neighbor in the memory bank.
requirements.quote: we compute its anomaly score as the distance to its nearest neighbor in the memory bank

requirements.stmt: Aggregate token scores to a document score via mean aggregation.
requirements.quote: To obtain document-level anomaly scores, we aggregate token-level scores across all tokens in the document. We use mean aggregation

requirements.stmt: Split data with 50% of normal documents as training; the remainder plus all anomalies form the test set.
requirements.quote: We use 50% normal documents as training data, the rest of data are set as testing including both normal and anomaly.

requirements.stmt: Evaluate with AUROC and AUPRC at both token and document levels.
requirements.quote: use AUROC and AUPRC as evaluation metrics

requirements.stmt: For the Grammar dataset, use 270 correct sentences as normal and 30 incorrect sentences as anomalous (10% anomaly rate).
requirements.quote: selecting 270 correct sentences as normal samples and 30 incorrect sentences as anomalous samples

requirements.stmt: Training is unsupervised/normal-only: no anomalous samples are used to build the memory bank.
requirements.quote: construct a memory bank of normal token embeddings and measure anomalies based on distance to the nearest normal neighbor

data.name: TokenCore benchmark datasets (SMS_Spam, Review, Grammar) with token-level labels
